newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark 1996 sales lifted by Belgacom.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark 1996 sales lifted by Belgacom.

text.p: Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark said on Tuesday its 23 percent increase in 1996 turnover was mainly due to income from partly-owned Belgian operator Belgacom.
"The rise in turnover is mainly attributable to the fact that Belgacom figured in Tele Danmark's accounts since April 1996," Tele Danmark said in a statement accompanying its 1996 results.
It said Belgacom's contribution to overall group turnover last year was 3.260 billion crowns.
Tele Danmark acquired a 16.5 percent stake in the semi-privatised Belgian telephone company in March 1996 .
In addition, Tele Danmark said turnover in Danish business rose 771 million crowns or 4.1 percent, of which 400 million crowns was directly related to mobile telephone activities.

Earlier the group posted a 1996 pre-tax profit of 5.067 billion crowns, down from 1995's 5.458 billion crowns, a result slightly better than analysts had expected on turnover 23 percent up at 23.304 billion crowns.

Tele Danmark said that although increased activity on the mobile telephone front had helped raise turnover, tariff cuts and promotional costs in a highly competitive market reduced earnings by 140 million crowns in 1996.
GN Store Nord's Sonofon is a key competitor to Tele Danmark in the Danish domestic mobile telephone market.
Tele Danmark said that a similar price war with lower margins on overseas telephone calls had forced income down by 210 million crowns last year.

It said that while increased competition had meant a 5.4 percent fall in income on overseas calls due to tariff cuts, domestic telephone calls had shown a 3.3 percent turnover rise in 1996, with an eight percent growth in traffic to and from abroad helping to offset market losses.
Tele Danmark said that activities abroad, mainly Belgacom, were responsible for 16 percent of group turnover.
